techniques.name: Add9 Chord Arpeggios
techniques.description: Andy Summers' signature technique of arpeggiated add9 chord voicings, using open strings and unusual fingerings to create a shimmering, ringing guitar texture unlike standard chord strumming

notes: C#m(add9): X-4-6-6-4-4 or with open strings X-4-6-1-0-0
A(add9): X-0-2-2-0-0 open voicing with natural add9
B(add9): X-2-4-4-2-0 with open high E as the add9
F#m(add9): 2-X-4-2-0-0 with open strings providing the add9 color
Each chord is arpeggiated, not strummed, for the characteristic sound
Open strings are left ringing to create sustain and harmonic richness
sequence: Form the add9 chord shape with the fretting hand
Pick individual strings in a consistent up-and-down pattern
Allow open strings to ring clearly into the next chord
Maintain strict rhythmic precision at the fast 150 BPM tempo
tips: The add9 voicings use open strings where possible for the ringing quality
Practice each chord shape individually before connecting them
Use a clean tone with chorus effect to approximate Summers' sound
Right hand pattern must stay absolutely consistent - use a metronome

techniques.name: Precise Right-Hand Picking
techniques.description: Fast, consistent alternate picking technique required to maintain the arpeggiated pattern at 150 BPM, demanding precise right-hand control and endurance

notes: The picking pattern uses strict alternate picking (down-up-down-up)
Each string is picked individually at sixteenth-note subdivisions
Right hand must remain relaxed to sustain the fast tempo for the full song
Consistent pick attack is essential for even volume across all strings
sequence: Begin with the pick on the lowest note of the chord
Alternate pick upward through the chord strings
Reverse direction at the top of the arpeggio
Maintain the continuous picking pattern through chord changes
tips: Use a thin to medium pick (0.60-0.80mm) for speed and flexibility
Keep the wrist loose and pivot from the wrist rather than the elbow
Practice at 100 BPM first and slowly increase speed
Take breaks if the right hand or forearm becomes tense
details.progression: Continuous arpeggio pattern over the chord progression

techniques.name: Chorus Chord Strumming
techniques.description: Transition from the arpeggiated verse pattern to fuller strummed chords in the chorus, requiring a shift in right-hand technique and dynamic level

notes: Chorus uses fuller chord voicings rather than the arpeggiated pattern
Dynamic shift from precise picking to energetic strumming
A, B, C#m, and F#m chords may use barre or open voicings
The shift provides welcome contrast after the constant arpeggio pattern
sequence: Transition from arpeggio picking to full chord strumming at the chorus entry
Use confident downstrokes on beat 1 of each chord change
Mix down and upstrokes for the energetic strumming pattern
Return to the arpeggio pattern when the verse returns
tips: Practice the transition from arpeggio to strum to make it seamless
Increase strumming dynamics noticeably for the chorus contrast
The chorus should feel like an energy release after the controlled verse
Use barre chord shapes for the chorus if open voicings feel too thin

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: The arpeggiated add9 chord pattern that establishes the songthe iconic vocal hook jangly guitar tone
notes: Guitar enters alone with the arpeggiated pattern before bass and drums join
Clean tone with chorus effect for the characteristic shimmer
Each chord rings into the next for harmonic overlap
Sets the rhythmic foundation for the entire song

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Verse continues the arpeggiated pattern with full band accompaniment, Sting's vocal melody riding over the rhythmic guitar texture
notes: Same arpeggiated pattern continues under the vocals
Bass and drums create a driving rhythmic foundation underneath
Guitar must remain consistent and steady as the rhythmic anchor
Do not vary the arpeggio pattern - consistency is key

sections.name: Pre-Chorus
sections.description: Building section with altered chord progression creating harmonic tension leading into the chorus release
notes: Progression shifts to build anticipation for the chorus
Dynamics may increase slightly through the pre-chorus
Same arpeggiated technique maintains continuity
Vocal melody rises in pitch to build tension

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: The dynamic release of the chorus with fuller strummed chords replacing the arpeggio pattern, supporting the signature vocal hook
sections.progression: A - B - C#m - A - B - F#m
notes: Full chord strumming replaces the arpeggiated pattern
Significant dynamic increase for the chorus impact
the signature hook is the song's most memorable moment
Return to arpeggio pattern when the verse returns

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: Extended outro with the arpeggiated pattern repeating as the vocal improvises over the progression, creating a hypnotic conclusion
notes: Returns to the arpeggiated pattern for an extended outro
Vocal improvisation and the iconic vocal hook repetitions over the pattern
Creates a hypnotic, cyclical feel as the song builds to conclusion
Fade-out ending with the arpeggio pattern still cycling

guitar.pickup: Single coils for bright, clear arpeggiated tone

effects.distortion: None for verses - clean tone is essential for the arpeggiated sections
effects.reverb: Short plate reverb for ambience without muddying the arpeggios
effects.other: Chorus effect (Boss CE-1 or similar) for the shimmering tone, flanger for select passages, compression for even note volume

beginner.title: Getting Started with Message in a Bottle
steps: Learn basic A minor, E minor, and D minor chord shapes
Practice simple arpeggiated picking across chord strings
Work on right-hand alternate picking at slow tempos
Develop finger independence for add9 chord shapes

intermediate.title: Mastering the Add9 Arpeggios
steps: Learn all four add9 chord voicings with open strings
Practice the arpeggiated pattern at gradually increasing tempos
Work on smooth chord transitions while maintaining the arpeggio
Master the transition from arpeggiated verse to strummed chorus

advanced.title: Full Performance at Tempo
steps: Play the complete song at full 150 BPM tempo
Develop right-hand endurance for the constant arpeggio pattern
Add chorus and flanger effects for authentic Summers tone
Perform the complete arrangement with dynamic verse-chorus contrast

commonMistakes: Picking pattern becoming uneven at the fast 150 BPM tempo
Not allowing open strings to ring freely in the add9 voicings
Losing the arpeggio rhythm during chord transitions
Making the chorus too similar in dynamics to the verse - contrast is essential
practiceRoutine: Warm up with basic alternate picking exercises on single strings
Practice each add9 chord shape individually with the arpeggio pattern
Work on chord-to-chord transitions at 100 BPM before increasing speed
Practice the verse-to-chorus dynamic transition repeatedly
Play along with the original recording for tempo and feel reference
focusAreas: Right-hand alternate picking speed and consistency at 150 BPM
Clean add9 chord voicings with open strings ringing clearly
Chord transition smoothness while maintaining the arpeggio pattern
Dynamic contrast between arpeggiated verses and strummed choruses
metronomeWork: Start the arpeggio pattern at 100 BPM with sixteenth-note subdivisions
Increase by 5 BPM increments until reaching full tempo at 150 BPM
Practice chord changes with quarter-note clicks to lock in the groove
Work on endurance by playing the full arpeggio pattern for 4-5 minutes continuously
